section1.title: What a game for two changes about an evening
section1.p1: A couple game looks like nothing at all. And yet it solves a very concrete problem: as a pair, you always end up circling the same subjects. The day, work, what's for dinner… A game imposes a frame, and that frame gives you permission to ask questions you'd never ask out of nowhere.
section1.p2: It's also why a game works better than a film when you genuinely want to reconnect. In front of a screen you're two people side by side looking elsewhere. Around a game you're two people looking at each other. You feel the difference within ten minutes.
section1.p3: The twelve games on this page run online, free, on one phone. Nothing to create, nothing to install, nothing to prepare.

section2.title: Which game to pick, depending on the moment
section2.intro: That's the real question. And the answer depends far less on your tastes than on the moment you happen to be in.
section2.row1Moment: A long drive or a train journey
section2.row1Pourquoi: It all works out loud, two options to weigh up and nothing to act out. Neither of you has to keep your eyes on the screen.
section2.row2Moment: An evening at home that is fizzling out
section2.row2Pourquoi: It takes no energy at all to start: a card drops and you answer. Three cards in, the evening is back on its feet.
section2.row3Moment: A moment that is just the two of you
section2.row3Pourquoi: A single deck running from suggestive to very direct, with the right to skip on every card. You set the limit, not the game.
section2.row4Moment: A lost bet, an evening to restart
section2.row4Pourquoi: Nobody picks the forfeit, so nobody feels targeted. One button, one spin, and it is settled.
section2.row5Moment: A proper evening for two, with no other screen on
section2.row5Pourquoi: The only one that lasts thirty minutes and can be won. A board, a dice, and a reason to keep going to the end.
section2.row6Moment: Dinner for two, or drinks before the guests arrive
section2.row6Pourquoi: Five minutes is enough, and every disagreement restarts the conversation on its own. The quickest one to pull out.
section2.row7Moment: A serious subject, without the heaviness
section2.row7Pourquoi: Every deal sets a gain against a price, so there is never a right answer. That is where you find out what the other one is willing to pay.
section2.row8Moment: A decision you have been putting off for months
section2.row8Pourquoi: The statements run from tonight's dinner to buying a house. The subject turns up on its own, neither of you had to raise it.

section3.title: Making a games night for two work
section3.p1: Four things separate a game you abandon after ten minutes from an evening you're still talking about the next day.
section3.conseil1Titre: One phone, set down between you
section3.conseil1Texte: Two screens means two attentions elsewhere. Our games are built to run on one device that you pass back and forth, and it completely changes the mood.
section3.conseil2Texte: A single notification is enough to break a moment that was just getting interesting. It's the most obvious tip on this list… and by far the most effective.
section3.conseil3Texte: A game for two only works if nobody feels cornered. Agree from the start that either of you can refuse a card without explaining: both card games have a forfeit for exactly that.
section3.conseil4Texte: The classic mistake is opening with the boldest game. Start with something that asks nothing of anyone, like a sentence to finish out loud: the rest follows on its own once the laughing has started.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Are these couple games really free?
faq.a1: Yes, all seven, from the first to the last. No account to create, no paid tier, no content unlocked after payment. Open the game's page and play.
faq.q2: Do I need to download an app?
faq.a2: No. Everything runs straight in your browser, on a phone or a computer. That's also what lets you start a game in ten seconds, right when the urge strikes.
faq.q3: What is the best game to play as a couple at home?
faq.a3: It depends on the evening! Truth or dare is the most versatile: it starts fast and stops whenever you want. Which one of us fits in five minutes and starts a conversation every single time. Would you rather works better when you feel like talking more than doing. The board game needs a proper half hour, but it's the only one you can win. The wheel is mostly for settling a bet. And the naughty version is for the moments when it's just the two of you.
faq.q4: Can we play remotely, each at home?
faq.a4: Yes. One of you opens the game, reads out loud on video and confirms for both. Truths, dilemmas and votes work perfectly at a distance, dares take a bit of imagination.
faq.q5: Are these games suitable for a couple who have just met?
faq.a5: Would you rather, which one of us, the forfeit wheel and the classic truth or dare, yes: none of them assume a shared history. The board game too, though its memory squares will feel a little thin early on. The naughty version, though, assumes you already know each other well: played too early it makes people more uncomfortable than amused.

section4.title: A game repairs nothing, but it opens doors
section4.p1: Let's be honest about what a game can do. It doesn't settle a fundamental disagreement, and it doesn't replace a conversation when one is needed. What it does very well is strip out the solemnity: it's the card asking the question, not you. That small shift is often enough to unlock a subject.
section4.p2: And if you want to go further than one evening, our couple tests raise the same subjects with a result at the end.
